title: Build a personal inventory from ordinary evidence

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: An inventory is a provisional account of evidence, not a character verdict. Strengths and limitations may depend on tools, time and support. An absent observation belongs under unknown, not zero.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional fortnight: Jo kept three appointments using reminders, arrived 12 minutes late once after an extra agreed care task, and missed one reminder because the device battery failed. A neighbor freely provided one lift; other journeys used the regular bus. Jo enjoys planning but fears disappointing people. No trauma history, health diagnosis or income facts are supplied.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Fill the nine headings with supported facts or unknowns. Rewrite “always reliable” and “hopelessly irresponsible” proportionately. Choose one practical adjustment rather than nine new goals.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person completes one task with extensive help and calls themselves either incapable or wholly self-sufficient. What more accurate account fits?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Three kept, one late and one missed reminder do not support either global label. Reminder use, care demands and transport help belong in the account; causal contributions remain tentative. Later fiction: Jo checks the battery before one new appointment and arrives on time, a single result. Partial: list only favorable evidence. Incorrect: invent painful history to fill every heading.
criteria: Both favorable and adverse evidence remain
Unknowns do not become identity claims

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Name the completed task, the person’s contribution and the actual help. One supported result establishes neither global incapacity nor independence in all settings.
criteria: Both favorable and adverse evidence remain
Unknowns do not become identity claims
